status: not implemented; bounded ordinary glue named for later explicit task
scope: A finite descriptor/packet ownership adapter for existing DEFAULT memory-copy hardware and a byte-faithful software guest consumer; not QEMU, DPDK port, networking stack or native virtio deployment.

interfaces.name: input/frame list
interfaces.rule: Complete real Ethernet frame bytes; capture actual next-run input or clearly label functional generated fixture. No invented source arrival/deadline. Segment source/destination by real layout; never pad to4096/64 just to fit existing experiment ABI.

interfaces.name: finite owner/mapping
interfaces.rule: Exclusive software issuer, no conflicting hardware owner; map both endpoint buffers in the DMA domain, reuse legal large/resident mappings. Labels A/B preserve lifetimes only; no guest isolation claim.

interfaces.name: ordinary executor
interfaces.rule: CPU direct copy; one-DMA direct copy; optional two-channel ordinary mapping of independent ready flows. For DMA use nonbatch DEFAULT, NUM_BYTES exact, SRC/DST exact, N_TRANS=1, batch disabled and controlled-launch disabled, preserve registers/VALID until handshake/completion.

interfaces.name: completion
interfaces.rule: Per-segment expected NEXT/DONE IDs and error/timeout checking; no B used publication before all accepted spans are done and global quiet/cache handoff permits CPU access. DONE alone does not certify bytes because backend no-error configuration exists.

interfaces.name: consumer
interfaces.rule: At safe CPU ownership, write/publish complete virtio header/used ID+length in source order; read original B cookie/address, verify complete packet and length plus neighbor guards. Only after consumer completion may B slot return to pool. A remains immutable until all reads finish; direct baseline may delay A completion relative to staged source.

interfaces.name: release
interfaces.rule: Stop issuer, account submitted/completed/cancelled/rejected work, global quiet; retain/quarantine on uncertainty; unmap/free only after checked release.

cache_scope.supported: One finite DMA phase, all participating payload buffers held away from CPU; global quiet before platform-local cache handoff, consumer and release. CPU can do safe separate bookkeeping/MMIO with no shared payload access.
cache_scope.not_supported_by_claim: Arbitrary per-slot simultaneous CPU payload access with another DMA active; coherent native vhost scheduling.
cache_scope.coldness: Use necessary cache ownership operations; do not copy the old mapping barrier IOMMU S1 flush into every retained-map phase. Page-table invalidation only when mapping semantics require.
cache_scope.CPU_baseline: Uses only actual CPU synchronization, never forced DMA cache/quiet costs.

causal_mapping.retain: Two endpoint lifetimes, full packet bytes, preposted destination capacity, source immutability until read retirement, used-before-consume order, legal direct single-copy ordinary path
Actual FPGA DMA sources/destinations both pass through same accepted shared IOMMU path; page walk and IOTLB counters only explanatory

causal_mapping.remove: Native guest/hypervisor isolation, real NIC, interrupts/eventfd, vhost socket/runtime, x86 timing and native physical DMA topology
Native simultaneous CPU producer/consumer overlap during DMA; finite global phases instead. No claim about streaming per-packet latency or throughput under native arrivals.

causal_mapping.effect: Eliminating native overlap can reduce/remove translation-performance opportunity; if ordinary finite baseline has no reachable avoidable residual, stop this projection rather than engineer pressure.

bounded_software_change_list: isolated experimental finite packet descriptor/input adapter
used/cookie lifecycle bookkeeping and full frame consumer
stop_if: Implementation requires new RTL/stream ingress, real VM runtime, new per-slot concurrent cache contract or changes source semantics; return concrete scope decision, do not expand automatically.
